quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: How can you tell if your rear tire has gone flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing noise from the rear of the bike.
The back end jerks from side to side.
You cannot accelerate.
The rear brake stops working.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: When your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. Riders rarely hear a tire fail.

questions.question: If one rider in a group wants to go faster than the others, what should the group do?

options.text: Let that rider go ahead and meet up at a planned spot later.
Speed up to match that rider's pace.
Split up so each rider can go their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let that rider go ahead and meet up at a planned spot later.
questions.explanation: If one group member wants to ride faster, let them go ahead and meet the group at a planned spot later.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which of these provides the best face protection?

options.text: Sunglasses
Windshield
Goggles
Face shield

questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute.

questions.question: A good lane position can help you do all of the following except:

options.text: Avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Go faster.
Set up for turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go faster.
questions.explanation: Your lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid blind spots, and set up for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: An advantage of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles is:

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You have a narrow view so you stay focused.
You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
You can follow the next vehicle's path more easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to maneuver.

questions.question: When securing a load on your motorcycle, place it:

options.text: As high as possible.
As low as possible.
On a sissy bar.
Only on one side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Place loads low on your motorcycle. Placing them high, such as on a sissy bar, raises the center of gravity and affects balance. Distribute loads evenly on both sides to prevent pulling the bike to one side.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Means they see you.
Guarantees they will yield to you.
Does not guarantee they see you.
Is not worth the effort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to guarantee a driver will yield to you. A driver may look at you and still fail to notice you.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, ride in the left portion of your lane because:

options.text: It increases your line of sight.
It decreases your line of sight.
It makes it hard to see beyond the vehicle.
It allows the other driver to speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases your line of sight.
questions.explanation: When preparing to pass on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane. This increases your line of sight and makes you more visible to drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: Which colors best help riders be seen?

options.text: Orange and red.
Green and blue.
Purple and gold.
Black and white.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange and red.
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?

options.text: One drink
Two drinks
Three drinks
Four drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: To find how many drinks remain, subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. In this case, 8 drinks minus 4 hours equals 4 drinks remaining.

questions.question: Where do motorcycle riders and other drivers most often have conflicts?

options.text: At intersections
On highways
On rural roads
In parking lots

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycle riders and other drivers have the most conflicts. Riders should be extra careful when approaching and going through intersections.

questions.question: Many over-the-counter drugs:

options.text: Make riding more dangerous.
Make riding safer.
Only affect your riding if you drink alcohol at the same time.
Have the same effect on every person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make riding more dangerous.
questions.explanation: Like alcohol, many drugs (including prescription medications, over-the-counter medications, and illegal drugs) have side effects that can make it harder to ride safely.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
Sit far back on the seat so you can keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle rather than support your body. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests to help balance.

questions.question: How often should a motorcycle rider check their mirrors?

options.text: Never
Once in a while
Often
More often than looking ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Often
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to know what is behind you and to spot possible dangers.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, it is usually:

options.text: Safest to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Dangerous to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Safest to cross by riding on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safest to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: When railroad tracks cross your lane at an angle, ride straight through your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle can be dangerous because you might end up in another lane.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, especially if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but still do not notice them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcyclist should tell the passenger to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Hold onto the seat.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on the motorcycle after you have started the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after you have started the engine.
questions.explanation: Give your passenger full safety instructions before the trip. Have them board after you start the engine. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold your waist, hips, or belt firmly. They must keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, make sure it has all of these qualities, except:

options.text: Meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
Fits snugly.
Has no defects.
Looks attractive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Looks attractive.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no visible defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that show rules like speed limits are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. Riders must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely so they can move.
Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
Use a lot of throttle to get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet because it could fall and cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
questions.explanation: On rough surfaces, grip the handgrips firmly. This keeps you in control of your motorcycle's direction.

questions.question: What does an experienced rider do?

options.text: Moves around in the lane as road and traffic conditions change.
Stays in the same part of the lane at all times.
Weaves back and forth in the lane to be more visible.
Rides only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Moves around in the lane as road and traffic conditions change.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists can use three different positions within their lane. Pick the safest position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest
On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use the rear brake only.
Use the front brake only.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: Their effects are stronger than when either is used alone.
They are less dangerous than when either is used alone.
Their effects are usually small.
Their effects usually cancel each other out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their effects are stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make it unsafe to ride. Some drugs become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.
